agenda: Review requests heard from carriers and prospects this week.
Compare sales pipeline feedback with support ticket trends.
Agree what evidence and fixes to bring to the next planning cycle.

chapters.title: Customer Requests and Workflow Friction
beats: Amara reports that 11 of 27 recent support requests mention bulk import or report speed, and recounts Harbor Logistics asking for proactive delay alerts and an API.
Priya asks whether the request count reflects separate carriers, and Amara explains that six carriers account for those 11 tickets.
Lucas distinguishes a slow report query from a broad reporting redesign and commits to a sample of slow jobs by Friday.

chapters.title: Pipeline Signals and ETA Trust
beats: Daniel says Acme Freight has 140 trucks, an approximately $60,000 annual budget, and a security review, but Tom worries that migration will be painful.
Daniel argues for a migration feature; Priya and Lucas push back on prioritizing a product build from one sales opportunity.
The group agrees that Daniel will bring three more prospect examples and Amara will compare existing customer import failures before planning.
Lucas says ETA accuracy is around 82 percent and calls for lane-level evidence before promising a model improvement.

chapters.title: Planning Inputs and Near-Term Owners
beats: Priya frames driver mobile app v2, ETA accuracy, and self-serve onboarding as proposals for the upcoming Q4 planning discussion, not settled bets.
Amara wants a narrow import fix immediately, while Daniel worries it will distract from Acme's migration conversation; Lucas proposes measuring the failure modes first.
The team agrees to prepare an evidence sheet and scope options rather than decide the Q4 roadmap in this sync.
Priya closes by assigning owners and deadlines for the planning inputs.
